discovery: Room-temperature tunnel magnetoresistance in magnetic tunnel junctions, including giant TMR in crystalline MgO barriers

nominees.name: Stuart S. P. Parkin
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute of Microstructure Physics, Halle, Germany

subfield: Condensed matter physics: spintronics and magnetism
motivation: In 1995 Miyazaki and Moodera independently showed large, reproducible tunnel magnetoresistance at room temperature in ferromagnet/insulator/ferromagnet junctions, turning Julliere's low-temperature curiosity into a working spin-dependent quantum tunnelling effect. In 2004 Parkin, together with Yuasa's parallel work, showed giant TMR in textured MgO(001) barriers, where coherent tunnelling through symmetry-filtered Bloch states yields magnetoresistance of hundreds of percent. These discoveries established spin-polarized tunnelling as a fundamental probe of electronic structure and created the magnetic tunnel junction, the core of every hard-disk read head since about 2005, of commercial MRAM and STT-MRAM now embedded in advanced CMOS nodes, and of spin-torque nano-oscillators and emerging neuromorphic and probabilistic computing elements. Few discoveries in condensed-matter physics combine such conceptual clarity with such broad technological impact. The 2007 Prize for GMR recognized metallic spin valves; the tunnelling counterpart deserves equal recognition.
